PROTECT

Protection starts with preparation.

The outside of a building needs a considered scope. We combine surface preparation, repairs, sealing and protective coatings, with rope access where suitable for the work.

Discuss this serviceSee our work

SOUND FAMILIAR?

Start with
what you can see.

  • Deteriorating facade coatings
  • Failed joints or sealants
  • A facade that needs repair and renewed protection

THE SCOPE

A system, step by step.

The written scope establishes what your particular building needs.

  1. 01

    Assess the surface

    Review the existing coating, defects and required access.

  2. 02

    Prepare

    Clean and prepare the substrate for the proposed repair and coating system.

  3. 03

    Repair & seal

    Address the scoped repairs and joint sealing before finishing.

  4. 04

    Apply & document

    Apply the protective coating and record the work for handover.

A FEW PRACTICAL ANSWERS

Before you
get started.

All common questions
Will the building need scaffolding?

Rope access can be an alternative for suitable facade work. The access method needs to be assessed for the building and scope.

Do you also handle the joint sealing?

Yes. Caulking and joint sealing can be included with the preparation and coating work in your written scope.
